pains.title: Profit on paper, no cash on payroll day
pains.problem: Clinicians get paid every week or two, but insurers and school districts pay later, and school work stops over the summer.
pains.how: Lucid's cash flow forecast, with payer mix tracking, shows the summer dip ahead so you can plan a reserve. Lucid works alongside your biller.

pains.title: Contractor or employee, and what each clinician costs
pains.problem: A contract clinician delivering the therapy you bill is doing core work, and the label in the agreement does not decide status.
pains.how: Your Lucid CPA reviews each clinician paid outside payroll against the IRS factors, shows cost and margin by clinician, and flags anything for your employment attorney.

pains.title: Low and falling payer rates
pains.problem: The payer sets the price, and a cut of a few percent on a thin margin can decide whether a group can hire.
pains.how: Lucid shows revenue and net cost per visit by payer, so a rate cut can be priced in dollars first. Lucid does not set rates or negotiate with payers.

faq_title: Speech therapy accounting questions owners ask

faq.q: Why is my speech therapy practice profitable on paper but short on cash?
faq.a: Your books count a session as revenue when it happens, but insurers and school districts often pay weeks later, and school work stops in summer while payroll does not. Lucid's cash flow forecast, with payer mix tracking, shows a shortfall ahead so you can plan a summer reserve.

faq.q: How do I know if I am losing money on Medicaid or a certain insurance?
faq.a: You need revenue and cost tracked by payer, not one total for the practice. Lucid sets up your books so you can see collections per visit and clinician cost per visit for each payer, and models what a rate cut would do to your monthly profit before it hits.

faq.q: Can I keep my speech therapists as 1099 contractors in my group practice?
faq.a: It depends on how much control your practice has over their work, not on what the paperwork calls them. If you set their schedule, assign the caseload and train them in your methods, they are more likely employees. Lucid shows you the cost of both options and flags anything to take to an employment attorney.

faq.q: How much money does my speech therapy practice lose to cancellations and no-shows?
faq.a: Insurers generally do not pay for a missed visit, so the loss falls on you, while clinician pay often continues. Multiply missed visits by your average collected fee per visit, then add the clinician pay you still owed. Lucid's reporting shows collected revenue and margin by clinician, so that math uses real numbers.

faq.q: Do I owe taxes or need to register in other states if my therapists provide teletherapy?
faq.a: It can depend on the state, and licensing is a separate question from tax. Lucid tracks teletherapy revenue and sales tax by state so you and your CPA can see where a filing may be needed.
